summary: Left Behind, Not Forgotten is a digital graphic novel and companion audio series that gives NASA's discarded hardware a voice. Since the 1960s, rovers, landers, descent stages and probes have been left on the Moon, on Mars and in deep space, yet most kids only hear about the missions still running today. In our story, each machine narrates its own chapter in first person, such as Viking 1, Spirit and Opportunity, or Pioneer 10, sharing why it was sent, how it worked, what it discovered and where it is now. Every chapter can be read as illustrated panels or heard as an audio episode. We use real NASA facts and images and list our sources in every chapter. Written for ages 9-14, the story includes alt text, transcripts and plain language so everyone can enjoy it. Our hope is that kids feel a real connection to these silent explorers and get inspired by the science they made possible. Team INGENIUM
details:
What it does and how it works

Left Behind, Not Forgotten: Voices of NASA’s Silent Explorers is a digital graphic novel for ages 9-14. It gives a voice to three pieces of NASA equipment that were left behind on their missions: the Viking 1 lander on Mars, the Pioneer 10 probe in deep space, and the descent stage of Apollo 11’s Eagle on the Moon. Each of the three chapters is told in first person by the machine itself, in six illustrated panels. Every chapter answers the same five questions: who am I, why was I sent, how did I work, what did I discover, and where am I now? Each chapter ends with an About page that gives its NASA sources, credits, and a text description of every panel.

Benefits

  • Young readers learn real mission facts through a story, not a textbook.
  • The fixed five-question structure makes the chapters easy to follow and compare.
  • The text descriptions of each panel make the book accessible to readers who cannot see the pictures.
  • All facts come from NASA sources, such as the NSSDCA records, the NASA mission pages, the Apollo Lunar Surface Journal, and Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter images. The illustrations are original artwork, so no NASA images are reproduced.

Intended impact

The project aims to change how young people see “discarded” space hardware. It is not junk. Viking 1 helped people see Mars as a place we can study. Pioneer 10 was the first spacecraft to cross the asteroid belt and take close-up pictures of Jupiter. Eagle’s descent stage serves as the launch pad that carried the first astronauts home from the Moon, and it still stands there as a monument to humanity’s first steps. We hope readers come away curious about the history of space exploration and about what we leave behind in space.

Tools and technology

  • Original stylised illustrations, designed by Team INGENIUM.
  • The book is laid out as a PDF with a clickable contents page and bookmarks for each chapter.
  • NASA’s public archives were the source of all mission facts.
  • got help from ai tools
  • Creativity
  • The machines narrate their own stories. The repeated closing lines (“I never left,” “I kept going,” “I’m still here”) give each one a distinct personality, and each line says something true about that mission.
  • The three chapters cover three different worlds: Mars, deep space, and the Moon.
  • Each chapter’s colour scheme matches its world.
  • The book treats “left behind” as meaning remembered, not abandoned.

Factors we considered

  • Audience: we chose simple, short text for ages 9-14, with six panels per chapter.
  • Accuracy: every fact comes from NASA sources, and the illustrations are clearly marked as stylised and not to scale.
  • Accessibility: every panel has a text description.
  • Scope: we focused on three well-documented missions that cover different environments, rather than trying to include everything.
